rule: Every rule value is declared for a layout study, with the publication it leans on and how that publication was read. The reading was done by an automated research pass on 2026-11-13; no person has re-read the passages. 'read' means the document itself was opened and the passage read in it; 'read by an automated reader' means the page was opened and the passage was extracted by a summarising tool; 'abstract only' and 'quoted by another' say so. No value comes from the maker of the machine or from a build processor.

build.why: the build of the layer screen and of the build screen (params/build-sim-case.json)

basis.says: walls or overhangs below 45 degrees from the build platform typically need to be supported

basis.source: Saunders, Design for metal AM - a beginner's guide, Renishaw, 2017
basis.says: overhangs of less than 45 degrees to the build plate require support (metals in general)
self-supported features no less than 45 degrees from the build plate (metals in general)

not_used.source: El Hassanin and Squillace, Metals 12 (2022) 2083, doi:10.3390/met12122083
not_used.says: AlSi10Mg walls print down to 30 degrees, with the roughest down-skin; 15 and 0 degrees fail
not_used.why_not: 45 degrees is the more cautious rule and the one of the orientation screen

not_used.source: Quickparts (3D Systems), Direct Metal Printing Design Guide, 2019, p. 20 and p. 14
not_used.says: aluminium: 35 to 50 degrees by surface size on p. 20, 50 to 55 degrees on p. 14

self_supporting_width_mm.value: an attached overhang up to 1.0 mm wide is left bare

basis.source: Saunders, Design for metal AM - a beginner's guide, Renishaw, 2017
basis.says: a horizontal overhang of 0.3 to 1 mm can self-support, though not recommended; more than 1 mm needs redesign or support

not_used.source: Lin et al., Applied Sciences 13 (2023) 3460, doi:10.3390/app13063460
not_used.says: AlSi10Mg cantilevers under 3.0 mm formed, with dross under all of them; 4.5 mm and more were stopped
not_used.why_not: formed is not to size; 1 mm is the cautious value

not_used.says: bridges under 1.2 mm supportless, flanges under 0.75 mm
not_used.why_not: the pictograms and labels of that page look swapped

self_supporting_width_mm.note: the screen takes the surface normal from a 0.5 mm Gaussian of the 0.25 mm grid and does not see a ledge much narrower than 1 mm as an overhang at all; the rule matters between that and 1.0 mm

slenderness_limit.value: none: the height over inscribed width of each support body is reported, not judged
slenderness_limit.note: no published limit for a block support was found

basis.source: Piscopo, Atzeni, Salmi, J. Mater. Eng. Perform. 33 (2024) 3978, doi:10.1007/s11665-023-09108-5
basis.says: AlSi10Mg block supports in Magics: hatching 0.68 x 1 mm, and 1 x 1 mm on a solid base; supports 5 mm high

basis.source: Yue et al., Results in Physics 44 (2022) 106204, doi:10.1016/j.rinp.2022.106204
basis.says: least porosity above AlSi10Mg block supports at 1.0 mm distance and 0.15 mm thickness

basis.source: Klanjscek and Kalin, J. Manuf. Mater. Process. 9 (2025) 200, doi:10.3390/jmmp9060200
basis.says: AlSi10Mg melt pools about 150 to 200 um wide on an EOS M290

basis.source: Van Cauwenbergh et al., Scientific Reports 11 (2021) 6423, doi:10.1038/s41598-021-85047-2
basis.says: AlSi10Mg melt pool width 189 +/- 15 um; power and speed not given

basis.source: Charan et al., EasyChair Preprint 10023 (2023), Fig. 6
basis.says: about 230 um at 350 W and 1100 mm/s, about 215 um at 1300 mm/s, read off a graph
basis.how_read: read; a preprint, not peer reviewed

tooth_contact_share_of_the_wall_line.value: 0.5: half of each wall's top line touches the part

basis.source: Poyraz et al., Solid Freeform Fabrication Symposium 2015, IN625 in Magics
basis.says: tooth top length = hatch / 2, base length = hatch
best teeth: top length 0.7 mm, base length 1.0 mm, base spacing 0.3 mm (0.54 of the line)

tooth_contact_share_of_the_wall_line.note: no source for aluminium was found: both are nickel alloy studies

could_not_open: Calignano, Materials and Design 64 (2014) 203, the usual reference for aluminium supports: closed access
Han et al., Materials and Design 160 (2018) 1080: abstract only
ISO/ASTM 52911-1 and any design guide of EOS or Eplus3D: not opened
default support values of Materialise Magics or Autodesk Netfabb: no source found
not_applied: horizontal round holes: guides let holes under 8 to 10 mm print without support (Renishaw 2017, Protolabs 2019, read); here the top arc of every hole is supported like any other surface
solid or denser supports under large overhangs for heat (Quickparts guide, read): one block pattern everywhere
an access gap for removal tools: no published value found; only straight lateral lines of sight are tested
powder escape from the support cells

process_for_the_time_estimate.note: the declared values of params/build-sim-case.json; the supports are assumed to melt at the energy density of the part
